name: Dull Brown
lede: Dull Brown is a descriptive name, not a pigment or a place: a brown with the brightness taken out, which the color books mention only in passing.

sections.title: The name
sections.body: Paterson's dictionary uses the phrase to define another word: *drab* is a dull brown or grey colour, or a dull light-brown or yellowish-brown, or simply lacking in colour [1]. In the same book *dull* itself means lacking in brightness or vividness [1]. So the name says two things at once: a brown hue, and a low, muted chroma. Close relatives in our list are [[brown]], [[french-beige]] and [[beige]], which Paterson defines as a light brown or yellowish grey [2].

sections.title: Where dull browns come from
sections.body: Gurney notes that red and green light add up to yellow, while the same two hues as pigments would mix to a dull brown or gray [3]. So mixing pigments of such hues is one route to a dull brown [3].

sections.title: A false reading
sections.body: Birren quotes the occultist C. W. Leadbeater, who claimed that a dull brown in a person's aura means avarice [4]. This is a claim of aura theory, not evidence; colors do not carry one fixed meaning, so the idea is only worth mentioning to set it aside [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: As a screen swatch, #876E4B measures about lightness 48.0, chroma 23.7 and hue angle 78 degrees in CIE LCH, so treat it as an approximation, not a pigment [5].

origin.named_after: the plain description: a brown that is dull
